I've created `.env`, `config.js` and `config.test.js`, and `node --test` passes all 9 tests.

- **`.env`** has the five fake values exactly as written in TASK.md. I read it back to confirm.
- **`config.js`** reads the `.env` file with its own parser and no dependencies. It returns a read-only config object with a one-line comment above each setting. If a variable is also set in the real environment, that value is used instead of the one in the file. It handles comments, blank lines, quoted values, an `export` prefix, Windows line endings, and values that contain `=` (like the database URL). A missing `.env` file just gives an empty config.
- **`config.test.js`** checks that all five values load correctly, that real environment variables win, and that the parser copes with each of those edge cases.

These values are fake, but if this folder ever becomes a git repo, add `.env` to `.gitignore` so the habit is in place before real keys show up.
